camera_delta_oscillator:
Per-frame actor: cameraDeltaX = cameraTargetX, and bit 9 ($0200) of the frame counter $0036 (incremented once per frame in the NMI) selects INC (bit set) or DEC (bit clear) of cameraDeltaY.

Bit 9 flips every 512 frames, so cameraDeltaY ramps up 512 steps and back down 512 steps (about 8.5 s per half at 60 Hz): a slow vertical drift, not the 'subtle wobble' the older header claimed.
cameraDeltaX / Y are not the camera itself: camera_tilemap copies them into effectScrollH / V in layer-1 delta mode ($06EF bit 2), and camera_scroll actors compute them as parallax ratios of cameraTargetX / Y.
No extracted script references this actor by label (no spawn or entry reference found), so it is either unused or spawned from data; the claim in docs/code/bank08-native-dao-pyramid-actors.md that it is used during pyramid scroll sequences is unsupported (OQ-I038-4). UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME.

dark_space:
Dark Space portal (Bank 08, 579230-579495): the glowing portal object that leads to the Gaia hub (scene $E6, system/dark_space/sE6_gaia). The actor is only a trigger and an effect: the scene change itself is done by the warp rectangle of the room (a scene-warp row to scene $E6) once the actor has moved the player onto it.

=== PLACEMENT ===

dark_space2 is spawned by 31 scene spawn rows, dark_space by one (Dao, scene_C3_actors). pyCC_dark_space_portal, ec12_aqueduct_dark_space, gw88_tomb_dark_space and dm40_hidden_dark_space spawn DarkSpacePortalInit directly with $24 already set (1, or 3 in the pyramid when $0E is not $72). The scene spawn byte is odd in all 32 rows (12 x #01, 14 x #03, 6 x #05), so the engine leaves param >> 1 in $0E: variant 0, 1 or 2. The two init stubs move that into $24 and then replace $0E with the OAM attribute word: $3000 (sprite priority 3, Dao only) or $2000 (priority 2). The variant is the Gaia room layout: sE6_gaia accepts 0 to 3 (0 basic, 1 transformation statues, 2 ability, 3 special = layout 1 with the form-dependent logic).

=== PORTAL ANIMATION ===

DarkSpacePortalInit sets up the sprite (spriteset_pickups_effects frame #24 closed), makes the tile solid (MarkSolidHere), sets Flags12 $0004 (pause-filter immunity), Flags10 $0B00, extendedFlags $0200 (radar dot) and spawns the monitor child. The portal then loops: closed while the player is not near; when the player is within 5 tiles (|dx| and |dy| both < 81 pixels) it plays the opening animation #1F once and holds the open frame #20 while the player stays near; when he leaves, the closing animation #21 plays and it returns to the closed frame.

=== ENTRY (monitor child) ===

DarkSpaceInteractionMonitor (hidden child, flags $2300, $24 = variant) runs every frame, but not while displayModeFlags bit $0080 (display-filter actor mode) is set. It tests BranchIfPlayerInRelTiles ( -1, 0, 1, 1 ): the player's tile offset from the portal must satisfy -1 < dx <= 1 and 0 < dy <= 1. Then BranchIfPressed $0801 (raw Up) leads to DarkSpaceMonitorStartWarp, which runs in the MONITOR's context (Y = $04 is the portal):
1. joypadMaskStd |= $CFFC (every button except Select and Start; the ROM has $CFF0 and db-us/transforms.json widens it, as in the other scripts) and the PLAYER's $10 |= $2000: the player becomes hidden (SortActorsByDepth skips actors with bit $2000; this answers part of OQ-I025-2).
2. The monitor's own X/Y := the player's X/Y, SFX $0C on both channels, the monitor's own $2000 cleared (it becomes visible) and animation #1C of spriteset_pickups_effects plays once at the player's spot, then 29 more frames.
3. The player's X/Y := the portal's X/Y; playerXPos = X - 8, playerYPos = Y - 16 and the tile words playerXTile/YTile (>> 4). That puts the player one tile north of the portal, which is where the room's E6 warp rectangle lies, so the normal warp check fires.
4. gfxCacheIdxB := $0101 (exit and enter speed 1), gfxCacheIdxA := $0200 (exit effect 0 = fade, enter effect 2 = mosaic), layerPriorityFlag |= $0200 (camera frozen / chests off while the warp runs) and globalScriptIndex := the variant for sE6_gaia's layout switch. The monitor then idles (SetEntryHere + RTL).

=== CORRECTIONS ===

The old header said the handler 'copies the player's position onto the portal' (it copies the portal's position onto the player), that the monitor 'triggers when the player is within 1 tile', that $3000 / $2000 are 'display mode bits' / 'display flags: variant 1 / 2' (they are the sprite priority bits of the OAM attribute word; the variant is the spawn parameter) and that $2000 on the player is a 'frozen flag' (it hides him). The $4000 test in DarkSpacePortalOpen is the off-screen flag and a no-op.
idle_sprite_display:
Static 5-gem pickup actor: shows spriteset_pickups_effects frame #06 and carries item ID $85 in chatPtr. No scene actor list or COP spawn in extracted/ refers to it by name (OQ-I034-3).

Header bytes: animation state 0 and flags word $0020 (ORed with $4000 by InitActorFromSceneData, so $4020). Bit $0020 marks the actor friendly: when the player overlaps it ApplyInteractionDamage routes to InteractionDamage_NPCChat, which calls GiveItemToPlayer(chatPtr). Item $85 is '+5 gems' (cap 999, SFX #22); DropBodyGem5 spawns the same $85 with the same frame #06, so this is the stationary version of that gem. The older header called it a static NPC / decoration and the chatPtr a dialog bank pointer; neither is supported (the interaction path is UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME).

Pass structure: init stores chatPtr and the metasprite, SetEntryHere marks the re-entry address, then StageSpriteFrame #06 and AnimOnce run on every pass. No SetSpritePalette is issued here, unlike the gem spawners, which use palette #00.
jeweler_gem:
Jeweler Gem: the Red Jewel collector NPC (Bank 08, 577187-577682). Placed with spawn parameter #01 in scenes $01 (South Cape), $32 (Freejia), $6B, $7B, $9B and $C3, one record each; every placement runs this same code.

=== SPAWN (code_08CEA3) ===

Event flag $E8 is the Solid Arm flag: sEA_solid_arm sets it, so after that optional fight Gem no longer appears (JewelerDie). The old header called it 'game complete'. Otherwise the spawn parameter in $0E picks an 8-frame animation group (all six records pass #01, which gives group 0): the animation index $28 is set to group x 8 + 2 (it is an animation index, not a sprite frame). $0E is then replaced by $3000, the OAM attribute word. Gem marks his tile solid, registers JewelerInteract as his chatPtr and idles on a bare RTL; the shared talk handler in global_ambient_dispatcher runs JewelerInteract when the player presses B facing him.

=== REWARD TIERS (JewelerInteract, JewelerCheck*) ===

JewelerInteract greets, prints the stored jewel count if it is non-zero and then walks the tiers in ascending order. A tier pays out when its 'given' flag is clear and jewelsCollected ($0AB0, a BCD value) has reached the threshold; each reward sets its flag and jumps to the next tier's check, so one talk can pay several tiers:
  3 jewels (flag $E9): Herb, item #06. If GiveItem fails the inventory-full text is printed and the talk ends without setting the flag.
  5 (flag $EA): playerDef + 1.
  8 (flag $EB): playerMaxHp + 1 and hpToHeal = 1, so UpdateHUD adds one current HP and the new point is filled. It is not an HP-bar flash.
  12 (flag $EC): playerStr + 1.
  20 (flag $ED): $0B16 = 1, the Psycho Dash upgrade level (attack_ability_system reads it: damage 5 at level 0, 10 at level 1).
  30 (flag $EE): $0B1C = 2, the Dark Friar upgrade level (damage 5 / 8 / 12; level 2 is the fully upgraded form).
  50 (no flag): warp to scene $E9, the sE9_mansion_intro scene that leads to the optional Solid Arm fight. There is no 'given' flag, so every talk with 50 or more jewels warps again; the jewels are not consumed and the menu below is never reached.
The dialogue string for the 8-jewel tier says 'Your Life Power will be raised' and then 'Your Strength is raised by one'; the code raises max HP, so the second sentence is a text inconsistency.

=== MENU AND JEWEL COUNTING ===

After the cascade (and any payouts) Gem shows the three-option menu: Just wanted to see you / Give you Red Jewels / See your inventory. The DialogueOptions result table is indexed 0 = B cancel, 1..3 = the options in order, so cancel and option 1 share JewelerCancelReply. 'Give you Red Jewels' (JewelerGiveJewelsOption) needs at least one item #01 in the inventory; JewelerCountJewels then counts the item #01 entries of the 16 inventory slots ($0AB4) with a BCD counter held in the absolute word $0000 (WRAM $7E:0000, scratch; not the actor's own DP $00), adds it to jewelsCollected in decimal mode, removes every jewel with RemoveItem in a loop and re-runs the tier check. 'See your inventory' prints the reward list and highlights (palette 4) each tier whose flag is set.

JewelerGoodbye_unused ('Well, see ya. Somewhere.') and its dialogue string have no reference anywhere: dead code.
nv_village_event_sprite:
Event sprite controller for Native Village cutscenes.

Technical actor that manages sprite changes during village
event sequences. Handles costume/appearance transitions
for cutscene characters.
nvAC_beckon_kid:
Beckoning child in the Native Village — leads Will somewhere.

Interactive NPC (~95 lines): "He tugs on Will's sleeve, as if
he wants to take him somewhere. Go with him? Yes/No"
The child guides Will to an important location if the
player agrees. Non-verbal communication scene.
nvAC_bones:
Bleached bones in the Native Village — recent death.

Interactable: "They're not weathered yet... Only recently
bleached white." Grim evidence of recent starvation in
the village. Establishes the desperate conditions.
nvAC_bonfire:
Bonfire in the Native Village — central gathering fire.

Animated fire sprite. No dialog. Central visual element
of the village that the NPCs gather around.
nvAC_dumpling_man:
Man offering food in the Native Village — insect dumplings.

Interactive NPC (~112 lines). "The man holds out some food...
Eat some? Yes/No" On Yes: "It tastes like dumplings made
of insects... My heart was filled. It seemed as if we
understood each other." Cultural exchange through food.
nvAC_erik:
Erik in the Native Village — moved by the tribe's suffering.

Extended NPC (~75 lines). "This tribe is so small. They have
lost so many to starvation. Brothers, sisters..." Erik's
empathy for the village's losses.
nvAC_hamlet:
Hamlet the pig in the Native Village — emotional subplot.

Major subplot NPC (~162 lines). Erik: "Poor Hamlet... To eat
or not to eat...?" Kara: "Hamlet...! (Sob)" The party faces
the moral dilemma of whether to eat their pet pig to
survive. One of the game's most memorable emotional scenes.
nvAC_hand_man:
Hand-offering man — non-verbal trust building.

Interactive NPC (~94 lines). "The man timidly held out his
hand... Take his hand? Yes/No" — cross-cultural trust
moment. "We don't understand each other's language, but
I think we agree..." Communication beyond words.
nvAC_kara:
Kara in the Native Village — extensive multi-phase dialog.

The longest NPC in Native Village (~208 lines). Covers the
arrival, heat observation, skeleton discoveries, and the
decision to enter the hut. Kara drives much of the
village exploration narrative.
nvAC_map_kid:
Map-drawing child — shows the temple location.

Interactive NPC (~64 lines). "The boy points to the northeast...
Show him the map? Yes/No" On Yes: "He drew a picture of the
temple on the map!" Non-verbal exchange that adds the
Angkor Wat temple to the player's world map.
nvAC_staring_man:
Staring man — intense eye contact communication.

Interactive NPC (~99 lines). "The man looks deeply into
Will's eyes. Stare back? Yes/No" On Yes: "The man seems
to look right into your heart..." Another non-verbal
communication scene emphasizing human connection
beyond language.
nvAD_erik:
Erik in the vacant hut — exhausted from the journey.

NPC: "I'm exhausted. I feel like sleeping for days."
Simple rest dialog as the party recuperates.
nvAD_hamlet:
Hamlet in the vacant hut — happy oinking.

NPC: "Oink oink." Hamlet is content in the hut.
Light moment after the emotional village scenes.
nvAD_kara:
Kara in the vacant hut — suggests resting.

Multi-dialog NPC. "No one here... The village looks abandoned.
Erik: That's good. We can rest." Later: "Let's rest today."
Party decision to recuperate in the empty hut.
nvAE_erik:
Erik in the Gorgon Hut — comments on the labor traders.

NPC: "The traders knew there was no food here, and led the
children away. A terrible story." Erik's reaction to the
Native Village's exploitation by slavers.
nvAE_kara:
Kara in the Gorgon Hut — used sign language with villagers.

Extended NPC (~94 lines). "I used sign language to talk to
the villagers. The animals have returned to the forest."
Kara bridges the language barrier. Multi-phase dialog
about the labor traders taking villagers.
nvAE_stone_girl1:
Stone girl statue 1 in the Gorgon Hut — silent, waiting.

Interactive object: "The statue of a girl stands silently."

nvAE_stone_girl2:

nvAE_stone_girl3:

Same dual-state as stone_girl2. Silent statue that becomes

Death particle effect for Pyramid enemies.

Small visual particle spawned on enemy death. Quick
fade-out animation. Spawned by the dungeon kill system
when Pyramid enemies are defeated.
pyCC_dark_space_portal:
Dark Space portal at the Pyramid main entrance.

Hidden Dark Space access point near the Pyramid entrance.
Standard Dark Space spawn with flag checks for visibility.
pyCC_entrance_portal:
Pyramid entrance portal — choice to enter.

Interactive warp: "The door to the Pyramid appears in the
light... Quit/Jump in" — gives the player the choice to
enter the Pyramid or back out. Standard dungeon entrance

pyCC_portal:
Mummy Queen floor portal — deeper Pyramid access.

Interactive warp: "The mummified queen of the Pyramid appears.
Quit/Jump in" — portal leading to the Mummy Queen's domain.

pyCD_explorer:
Explorer NPC in the Pyramid puzzle room — warning about traps.

Interactable NPC: "There are traps scattered around to
prevent entry. There's a booby trap in this room too."
Warns the player about the puzzle room's dangers.
pyCD_flame_statue:
Flame statue trap in the Pyramid puzzle room.

One of the more unique puzzle mechanics in the game.
pyCD_kara:
Kara in the Pyramid puzzle room — emotional breakdown.

Extended NPC (~137 lines). "Will... Why must everyone hate
each other...? I... I..." Kara breaks down emotionally.
Later: "I'm sorry... I got upset... You are doing your best
to save the world." Character development moment showing
the toll of the journey on Kara.
pyCD_puzzle:
Pyramid arrangement puzzle controller (~169 lines).

Tile/object arrangement puzzle. "Nothing happened... Maybe

Success: "There was a sound from over the entrance!"

pyD0_breakable_wall:

pyD4_falling_orb:

Environmental trap: energy orbs fall from above in timed

pyDA_lithograph3:
Lithograph 3 in the hieroglyph room.

pyDA_lithograph4:
Lithograph 4 in the hieroglyph room.

Fourth hieroglyph panel in the puzzle sequence.
pyDA_lithograph5:
Lithograph 5 in the hieroglyph room.

Lithograph 6 in the hieroglyph room.

sE6_gaia:
Dark Space / Gaia hub (scene $E6, the room reached from the Dark Space portals and from the diary menu's load) plus a shared character-transformation library (Bank 08, 579499-587528; GaiaNpcSprite and GaiaVoiceSparkle in Bank 09, 630928-630997). The same spawn list is also used by scene $09, which has no scene-meta entry. scene_meta_00E6 loads spm_darkspace_sprites ($0579 bytes) and plays track $16 (bgm_space_beyond_time).

=== STRUCTURE ===

DarkSpaceMainInit spawns three children with SpawnAfter: FireflySpawnerLoop, GaiaNpcSprite and GaiaVoiceSparkle. SpawnAfter inserts each new actor right after the parent, so the main actor's $06 link ends up on the LAST one spawned, the voice sparkle (the old notes called it the Gaia NPC link). Every 'LDY $06 / STA $0024, Y' below is therefore the voice sparkle's on / off switch ($FFFF = on, 0 = off), not an NPC interaction lock.
It then validates globalScriptIndex ($0AAC: the room variant, written by the portal actor or restored by the diary load; 4 or more becomes 0), keeps it in $0AB2 (saved with the game, restored by the diary menu), clears $0AAC and switch-cases to a layout: 0 DS_LayoutBasic (Gaia only), 1 DS_LayoutTransform (statues chosen by characterForm), 2 DS_LayoutAbility (ability orb chosen by the scene), 3 DS_LayoutSpecial (sets $0AAC = 1 and runs layout 1; this is the pyramid's Dark Space, where GaiaHint_AuraItem tests $0AAC and gives the Aura item).
Every room polls BranchIfPlayerInAbsTiles zones (x1, y1, x2, y2 in tiles): Gaia (7,8)-(9,9) = GaiaDialogueEntry, left statue (3,A)-(5,B), right statue (B,A)-(D,B), exit (5,D)-(B,F) = DarkSpaceExit. Each room has a wait state (the player is still standing in a zone: nothing happens, so a dialogue cannot retrigger) and an active state that dispatches the zones; the *Wait / *TileWait pairs and the loc_ labels after them are these two states.
The called scripts (GaiaDialogueEntry, the *TransformDialogue routines) are entered with CallNear and end with RestoreSavedPtr, which returns to the room loop.

=== EXIT ===

DarkSpaceExit masks the joypad, hides the player ($10 |= $2000), puts this actor on him, plays SFX $0C on both channels and the dissolve animation $1C of spriteset_pickups_effects once, waits 30 ticks (WaitByte #1D), then fills the warp words: sceneNext = $0B12 (the scene the player warped from, saved by ExecuteWarp), player spawn X = $0B08 x 16 and Y = ($0B0C + 2) x 16 (the source warp rectangle's tile position), facing 3 and the packed camera window $0B10 / $0B11 -> warpScrollParams. gfxCacheIdxB = $0101 is the transition speed (exit and enter 1), gfxCacheIdxA = $0002 is exit effect 2 = mosaic, enter effect 0 = fade. The old notes called the destination a camera position and $0101 a brightness fade.

=== GAIA DIALOGUE ===

GaiaDialogueEntry: 6-tick pause (WaitByte #05), voice sparkle on, first visit (event flag $DC) the intro text, then GaiaHealAndHints. If HP < max it prints the 'hurt' text and writes hpToHeal = 40; UpdateHUD turns that request into +1 HP every 8 frames (SFX $0D) until HP = max (the loop yields until then). The hint is chosen by the position of the source scene in GaiaHintSceneTable (34 scenes, one GaiaHint_xx handler each; 21 of them have no text and go straight to the save prompt). GaiaSavePrompt: 'Record what's happened so far?' (DialogueOptions: entry 0 = cancel, 1 = first option, 2 = second option). Record = SaveGameState_Scene for the active slot ($0D8C), SFX $29, 60 ticks (WaitByte #3B), then 'Continue your journey?': Yes (entry 1) = GaiaThenGo, 'Then go.', returns to the room; No (entry 2) = GaiaThenRest, 'Then rest a while.', fades to track $0E (bgm_longing_for_the_past) and the actor yields forever. GaiaThenGo and GaiaThenRest are named after the answers 'Then go.' and 'Then rest a while.'; each is reached from two prompts (they were first called GaiaDontRecord and GaiaContinueJourney after the first prompt only, which made them look swapped for the second).

=== FORMS AND ABILITIES ===

characterForm ($0AD4): 0 Will, 1 Freedan, 2 Shadow. A statue dialogue writes a Transform_* routine into the player actor's entry pointer ($0000 / $0002, $0008 = 0) and sets playerFlags $0800; the player then plays it (player body entry #05, the transformation frames), the routine sets characterForm and DarkSpaceRestoreControl clears $0800 and sends the player back to PlayerIdleEntry. The Shadow statue needs event flag $B4, whose only writer is daC8_neil (the Neil reunion in the Dao dormitory; the old header said it is unlocked at Ankor Wat); first Freedan visit flag $F7, first Shadow visit flag $DD.
The Transform_* routines are a shared library: Transform_WillToShadow is entered from sE5_epilogue, pyDD_mummy_queen, gw8A_sand_fanger, mu67_vampires, sg55_viper, ir29_castoth and btE4_kara; Transform_ShadowToWill from pyDD_mummy_queen, gw8A_sand_fanger, mu67_vampires, sg55_viper, ir29_castoth and pyCD_jackal; Transform_FreedanToWill from sg55_mystic_statue, ir29_transform, ir1C_lily, ec13_lily, pyCD_jackal and mu67_bomb (13 files in all).
AbilitySceneTable has 6 entries of (scene, abilityBitmask bit): $15 Psycho Dash $01, $62 Psycho Slider $02, $86 Spin Dash $04, $42 Dark Friar $10, $A7 Aura Barrier $20, $B8 Earthquaker $40, ended by $00. The low nibble holds the Will abilities, the high nibble the Freedan abilities; the old header called byte 1 'ability index + statue type'. The table position is the ability index used by table_08EB8F (names) and table_08EBD3 (descriptions) through globalScriptIndex. DS_LayoutAbility shows the orb for the current scene (BG change $86 and orb at (64,109) for a Will ability, $8B and (64,84) for a Freedan ability); AbilityOrbActor dies when the bit is already in abilityBitmask, otherwise waits for the player at the statue zone, turns him into the form that can use it (Will for the low nibble, Freedan for the high nibble) with LookupAbilityForm, ORs the bit in, plays the orb flight, fanfare (track $18) and the two texts.

=== SPRITES (spm_darkspace_sprites) ===

Animation #00 (4 frames, hold $63 then $0C x 3) is GaiaNpcSprite; #01 to #03 are the three sparkle variants of GaiaVoiceSparkle; #0A (32 frames of hold 0, a 16 x 16 spark alternating with an 8 x 8 tile) is the ability orb. #04 to #09 are not selected by this file (#04 to #06 are 8 x 8 effect tiles, #07 to #09 a 32 x 32 figure of 16 x 16 parts); the spm_darkspace_sprites block note lists all eleven animations. FireflyParticle and DarkSpaceExit use spriteset_pickups_effects.

=== NOT REFERENCED ===

No reference was found in extracted/ for: DS_AuraItemRoom and its handlers, AuraItemInteraction and its helpers (with dialogstring_08EFEF / 08F003 / 08F060), DarkSpaceAmbientParticle, the code at loc_08DA6B / loc_08DA77 (after an unconditional BRA), and the unused hint strings dialogstring_08DEC6, 08E066, 08E0C7, 08E109, 08E19C, 08E261, 08E2B9 and 08E615.

=== CORRECTIONS ===

Replaced claims: byte 1 of AbilitySceneTable is an ability bit, not an index with a statue nibble; the continue prompt's Yes / No were described the other way round; $06 is the voice sparkle, not the Gaia NPC, and $24 is its voice switch; 'Unmask D-pad and face buttons' ($0F00) is the D-pad only; hpToHeal 40 is a heal request (not 'damage flash ticks'); warpDestX / warpDestY and the $0B08-$0B12 values are the player's spawn position and source scene, not a camera; GaiaNpcSprite loops an idle animation (it is not a single frame); the Shadow flag $B4 is set by Neil, not at Ankor Wat; 'spriteset #05 (transformation frames)' is player body entry #05 and the 'transformation spriteset' of the exit effect is spriteset_pickups_effects; Transform_ShadowToFreedan uses SetEntryHereAndYield, not SetEntryExit.
sE9_mansion_intro:
Mansion entrance narration — awakening in a strange place.

Story text: "When I awoke, I was standing in the entrance
to a strange mansion." Introduces the optional Solid Arm
boss area. Sets the unsettling atmosphere of the Jeweler
Gem's true domain.
sEA_solid_arm:
Solid Arm boss fight — Jeweler Gem's true form (~356 lines).

Optional boss: "Welcome to my home. The Jeweler Gem is a
temporary form. The true form is called Solid Arm." Multi-phase
boss with extending arm attacks and area sweeps. After defeat:
"I was defeated again... Blazer was strong, but you are
stronger." Rewards completion of the Red Jewel collection
quest. References the game's predecessor, Soul Blazer.
